Print and summarize sparse regression fits

Source: R/model_summary.R, R/sparseglm_methods.R
model_summary.Rd

Concise S3 displays for L0glm.fit(), L0nnpois() and sparseglm() results, including negative-binomial, multinomial and Cox models.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'L0glm_fit'
print(x, digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L), ...)

# S3 method for class 'L0glm_fit'
summary(object, ..., mu_floor = 0, beta_true = NULL, r2_mu_floor = 0.1)

# S3 method for class 'summary.L0glm_fit'
print(
  x,
  digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L),
  max.rows = 20L,
  max.cols = 6L,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'sparseglm'
print(x, digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L), ...)

# S3 method for class 'sparseglm'
summary(
  object,
  ...,
  mu_floor = object$mu_floor,
  beta_true = object$beta_true,
  r2_mu_floor = 0.1
)

# S3 method for class 'summary.sparseglm'
print(x, digits = max(3L, getOption("digits") - 3L), ...)

Arguments

x

A fitted model, comparison or corresponding summary object.

digits

Significant digits for printed numeric values.

...

Reserved for additional method arguments; currently unused.

object

An L0glm_fit model or sparseglm comparison.

mu_floor

Nonnegative scoring-only mean floor. Model summaries default to zero, matching stats::logLik() and the criterion methods. Comparison summaries use the floor stored by sparseglm() to match tuning scores.

beta_true

Optional true coefficients for recovery metrics, with the same dimensions as the returned coefficients, including any intercept. Comparison summaries default to their saved truth. Use NULL to omit it.

r2_mu_floor

Count-mean floor used only for R-squared working weights, default 0.1. See L0glm.metrics().

max.rows, max.cols

Maximum coefficient rows and response columns shown by print.summary.L0glm_fit(), default 20 and 6. Positive integers or Inf. Only nonzero or mandatory coefficient rows are displayed. These limits do not subset the coefficients retained in the summary.

Value

summary() returns a list of class summary.L0glm_fit or summary.sparseglm. Both contain metrics and model dimensions. Model summaries also contain the full sparse coefficients, selected row indices, dispersion/theta, screening diagnostics when used, and a compact convergence table. print() methods return their input invisibly.

Details

Printing a fitted object uses its stored metadata and coefficients; it does not evaluate likelihoods or refit a model. summary() calls L0glm.metrics() to obtain likelihood, deviance and information criteria, optionally including recovery metrics. The full original-dimension sparse coefficient matrix is retained in the model summary. Coefficients are point estimates; standard errors and Wald tests are not calculated for the selected penalized model. Screened fits display the screening method, number of rounds, chosen round, batch size and screening thread count; summaries retain their complete screening diagnostics.

Convergence counts use the last recorded pass for each stage and channel, rather than counting intermediate grouped-selection passes as final failures. Missing backend diagnostics remain unavailable. The printed dispersion is the stored fitting scale; the profiled Gaussian likelihood scale can differ, as described in model_criteria. NB summaries also retain theta and its estimation flag. Cox and multinomial do not display an ordinary dispersion.

Comparison summaries retain the complete metrics table, including timings, tuning metadata and explanatory notes for unavailable or failed methods. Their printed tables show essential scores, plus recovery measures when truth is available. No fitted models or adaptive pilots are recomputed.

See also

L0glm.metrics(), model_criteria, sparseglm()

Examples

set.seed(4)
X <- matrix(rnorm(240), 60, 4)
y <- 2 * X[, 1] + rnorm(60)
fit <- L0glm.fit(X, y, lambda="gic", parallelize=FALSE)
print(fit)
details <- summary(fit)
print(details, max.rows=10)
details$metrics
comparison <- sparseglm(X, y, method=c("L0glm","lasso"), nlambda=4,
                        lambda=list(L0glm=c(10,4,2)))
summary(comparison)
